```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
```

## The setup

* You are an analyst at a luxury jelly e-commerce retailer with a “Jelly of the Month Club.”
* The retailer is testing whether introducing a testimonial from Clark Griswold on the sidebar of the webpage will (1) increase conversions to the JMC and (2) increase the average cart amount of those who purchase.

## Getting to know the data

Read in the `banner_ad_results.csv`

```{r}

jelly <- read.csv("banner_ad_results.csv")

head(jelly)

```

Do some things to get to know what data we have available:

* as a whole
* some stuff about individual columns

```{r}

mean(jelly$convert)

mean(jelly$cart_amount)
sd(jelly$cart_amount)

hist(jelly$cart_amount)

```

Our data has been dirty at this company before with duplicate transaction ids.  This should be unique for every transaction (row). Prove that we have only unique `trans_id`s

```{r}

jelly |> 
  group_by(trans_id) |> 
  summarise(count = n()) |> 
  arrange(desc(count))


```

How many `trans_id`s are there per `group`?

```{r}

jelly |> 
  group_by(group) |> 
  summarise(n = n())

```

## Analyzing the effects of the ad

**Is the testimonial ad worth it based on *<u>cart amount alone</u>*?**

Some additional context:

* The jelly site sees about 6500 transactions per month.
* The monthly cost to keep the testimonial is $500

```{r}

mean = jelly |> 
  group_by(group) |> 
  summarise(
    avg_cart_amount = mean(cart_amount),
    avg_convert = mean(convert)
  )

print(45.76*6500)
print(46.08*6500)

```

*What assumptions have to be made to make this recommendation?*
